scope: owned src/hmt_pg_patterns Python; SQL contracts separately bind authority and atomicity

P10-01.mapping: Production code avoids dynamic eval/exec/compile; explicit bounded control and exception contracts are checked by fresh analyzers and the complete loop-site inventory. Dependency internals are outside the owned control-flow claim.

P10-02.mapping: Every observed production loop is bound to an explicit reviewed finite collection/limit and a current executed witness; no unobserved loop is admitted.

P10-03.mapping: Python allocates dynamically; the platform mapping is finite input, packet, frame, row, pool and retry budgets, not a claim of no heap allocation after initialization.

P10-04.mapping: Fresh physical-line structural check requires every function<50 and module<150 lines; argument and nesting limits remain active.

P10-05.mapping: Runtime contracts use explicit exceptions and strict closed validation rather than optimizable assert statements; independently asserted negative and positive behavior supplies check evidence.

P10-06.mapping: Authority snapshots are deeply immutable; caller-owned nested values are detached and no production global mutation statement is permitted.

P10-07.mapping: Public parameters are revalidated at execution boundaries; failed transactions and uncertain teardown outcomes remain classified and cannot silently succeed.

P10-08.mapping: Python has no user preprocessor in this branch; dynamic SQL values stay parameter-bound and identifiers come from a closed quoted allowlist.

P10-09.mapping: Python references replace pointer arithmetic: exact types, immutable snapshots and copied input bytes prevent caller mutation from changing admitted authority.

P10-10.mapping: Fresh Ruff, mypy and Pyrefly run with an explicit pinned analyzer interpreter and must all succeed on the same production source; native CI42 retains its independent checks.
